entries.migration_impact: New bootstraps and import-payload runs omit bytecode. Repos that already committed scripts/plate/__pycache__/ may delete those paths and add local gitignore rules (#1460).
entries.agent_notes: After upgrading plate-core, re-run import-payload only if you need refreshed scaffolding; remove any previously copied __pycache__ under scripts/plate/ from git history if present.

entries.migration_impact: New repositories created via `gh plate bootstrap` or `gh plate import-payload` now receive a root `.gitignore`. Existing adopters without one can copy it in; existing `.gitignore` files are left unchanged by conservative/safe strategies and can be merged by hand.
entries.agent_notes: The payload `.gitignore` is intentionally modest, not a copy of plate-core's 217-line root ignore file. It must include `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `.venv/`, and `.env`. The separate payload __pycache__ copy-filter is #1459 and is not handled here.

entries.migration_impact: New greenfield bootstraps receive the same unreleased README as the #996 import seed. `conservative` and `safe` import skip an existing file at that path (including #996-seeded or custom text) instead of raising a payload conflict or escape hatch. Older template payloads without this file still get the adoption seed on import.
entries.agent_notes: Template README must stay byte-identical to `MINIMAL_UNRELEASED_README` in import_payload so identical seeded copies skip under conservative. `_seed_releases_layout_if_missing` is a no-op for the README when the payload manifest includes the path; it still mkdir-backfills pre-#1461 templates.
Human-readable gh plate agents delegate output once again includes the task, delegation prompt, and Copilot/CLI invocation hints after the 'Delegating to:' line.

entries.migration_impact: Downstream repos gain a Hardening label, issue template, and PR type. Hardening PRs require a release fragment with change_type "hardening". Hardening fragments route to patch unless marked breaking; they never auto-select minor the way feature fragments do. Real defect corrections remain Bug and new capabilities remain Feature.
entries.agent_notes: Use Hardening only for standalone executable test coverage, CI reliability, isolation, or safety work with no new product capability. Real defect corrections stay Bug; new capabilities stay Feature; executable tests must never be classified as Documentation. Hardening PRs require a release fragment and a linked issue, and must not be self-merged.
migration_guidance: 1. Sync labels from .github/labels.yml (or let bootstrap create Hardening on next apply).
2. Copy .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/hardening.yml and the updated PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md into your repo.
3. Update any local label-check or PR-type gate lists to include Hardening.
4. Use change_type "hardening" for standalone test, CI reliability, isolation, or safety fragments; keep breaking changes marked breaking so they still route to major.

entries.agent_notes: The tool branch now reads repo from args.get("repo") matching the pattern used by all other tool branches in _handle_tools_call.
